goldfinch.story: A tiny goldfinch seems alive until a delicate chain changes the feeling; the yellow wing's scratched paint reveals Fabritius's craft. Physical scale is explicit, the museum setting is an illustrative reconstruction, not an actual room photograph.

scenes.intent: First museum view: a 33.5 cm high panel is tiny against a human-scale wall; title and artist appear together.
Visitor approaches the small framed panel; gallery geometry scales consistently, not an enormous wall-sized painting.
Close to the frame: the little goldfinch becomes legible before the image enters the painting.
The bird's face and posture feel alive; pause on the real painted expression.
The red facial mask and alert eye show Fabritius's delicate optical illusion.
Yellow wing paint scratched with brush handle: museum-documented material technique.
Reveal the fine chain that changes the emotional reading of the tame bird.
The whole bird and feeding box are reunited in the original panel, without overlay.
Exit the painting into the same reconstructed museum wall, restoring the actual small scale.
End in the original room perspective: an intimate small panel rather than a monumental canvas.
